heroHeadline: China Blocks Meta's $2B Manus AI Deal; ByteDance $5.6B Huawei Chip Order Seals China's Complete AI Decoupling
heroSubtitle: Beijing's NDRC vetoed Meta's acquisition of Manus AI (April 27–28), establishing that AI systems built on Chinese soil are sovereign assets regardless of corporate domicile — extending the April 26 capital-flow controls into asset-transfer controls. ByteDance committed $5.6 billion to Huawei's Ascend 950PR (April 29) — the largest non-Nvidia AI chip order ever — as Alibaba and Tencent joined the scramble. Chinese vendors are forecast to ship 2.123 million high-end AI accelerators in 2026 (+136% YoY), with Huawei targeting 50% domestic market share. The week of April 24–30 marks the emergence of a complete, sovereign Chinese AI ecosystem across models (DeepSeek V4 on Huawei), hardware (Ascend 950PR mass production), capital flows (US investment barred from AI startups), and corporate ownership (Manus veto) — simultaneous decoupling across every dimension.
